name: JevShield AI Anti-Spam for Forms
author: elpx

sections.description:
Bot checks and message filtering address different problems. A visitor can pass a CAPTCHA and still submit an unsolicited sales pitch or a suspicious message. JevShield checks message content alongside your existing bot protection.

JevShield uses semantic AI to read what was actually submitted and judge message intent: genuine inquiry, unsolicited pitch, or outright scam. Visitors never see a puzzle, checkbox, or challenge.

  • Checks message intent: Flags patterns associated with unsolicited SEO pitches, guest-post offers, extortion, crypto scams, and phishing. Automated classification can make mistakes.
  • No extra puzzles: This plugin does not add a CAPTCHA or checkbox to your forms.
  • Buyer intent signals: Genuine inquiries are scored 0–100 so you can spot high-intent buyers (budget, timeline, booking requests) instead of letting them drown in noise.
  • Fail-open handling: If checks fail or quota is exhausted, JevShield allows the submission to continue. Other plugins and form validation may still prevent delivery.
  • Observe first: New installations start in Observe only mode. Messages are classified and use quota, but JevShield does not block them. Switch to Block high-confidence spam after reviewing results. Existing configured installations retain blocking when upgraded.
  • Filterable detection logs: Open your JevShield account and filter by Uncertain — review. Review verdicts are allowed through by this plugin. These logs are not a moderation inbox and cannot recover undelivered mail.
  • Reported actions: Supported integrations report their allowed, blocked, or error-allowed decision. A successful report records JevShield’s action, not final inbox delivery; unavailable reports remain unknown.
  • Broad compatibility: Contact Form 7, WPForms, Elementor Pro Forms, and native WordPress Comments.

External Service

This plugin connects to JevShield Cloud API (https://jevshield.com/api/v1/check) to classify submitted form content and protect your website from spam.

  • Service Provider: JevShield Cloud (https://jevshield.com)
  • What data is sent: The plugin sends selected message/subject text, sender name, email address, site URL, and form identifier over HTTPS when a configured integration submits a check. The API key is sent in an authentication header. It also sends a check ID, report token, action, and action reason to the corresponding /api/v1/report endpoint to record the plugin’s decision. Selected free-text fields may contain information entered by visitors; do not collect passwords or payment data in them.
  • Connection checks: Opening the settings page verifies your key and retrieves quota from the check endpoint without submitting message content. Quota warnings store only a credential/endpoint fingerprint in WordPress, not an extra copy of your key.
  • Logs: Cloud detection logs contain classification and execution metadata. Message content storage depends on your account’s log-content setting. See the privacy policy and disclose this processing to your visitors. Observe mode still sends messages and uses quota.
  • Terms of Service: https://jevshield.com/terms
  • Privacy Policy: https://jevshield.com/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/jevshield-ai-anti-spam/, or upload the ZIP file directly through WordPress Admin > Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Navigate to Settings > JevShield AI in your WordPress admin menu.
  4. Enter your JevShield API key (get a free key at https://jevshield.com/account) and save settings.
  5. Leave Protection Mode > Observe only selected while testing. Submit a genuine inquiry and a test sales pitch, then check the detection logs in your JevShield account and your actual inbox separately.
  6. Switch to Block high-confidence spam when you are satisfied with the results. You can return to Observe only at any time. If upgrading from the legacy FormShield ZIP plugin, deactivate that plugin before enabling this one and copy your API key/settings; running both may double-check or block submissions independently.
sections.faq:
Does this require a JevShield account?

Yes. You need an API key from https://jevshield.com to enable cloud semantic spam checks. A free tier with 100 checks per month is available.

What happens if the JevShield API is unavailable?

JevShield does not block the submission when the API cannot be reached, returns an error, or gives an invalid response. Other form plugins, validation rules, or mail delivery problems can still affect the submission.

Will it block legitimate customer messages?

False positives are possible. Successful checks return allow, review, or block. In Observe only mode this plugin does not block any result. In Block mode it blocks only block verdicts meeting your spam threshold; review verdicts continue through the form. We recommend running in observation mode for the first week to confirm the verdicts match your judgment. Use filterable detection logs in your JevShield account to inspect Uncertain — review results; this is not an email recovery queue.

What happens when quota runs out?

JevShield checks are paused and forms continue through this plugin. An administrator notice links to your account and plan options. The settings page verifies current remaining quota. After quota resets or you upgrade, refresh this page; successful checks with available quota also clear the warning. Observe mode consumes the same check quota as Block mode.

What is the buyer intent score?

Alongside the spam verdict, the API can return a 0–100 intent score based on commercial signals such as budget, timeline, and project scope. This is an estimate, not a guaranteed buyer. Account-level routing features are separate; the WordPress plugin does not automatically redirect visitors to a meeting page.

Is there a free plan?

Yes. The free tier includes 100 checks per month, no credit card required. Paid plans start at $9/month for 5,000 checks. See https://jevshield.com/pricing for details.

Do I still need my CAPTCHA?

You can keep it. CAPTCHAs and Turnstile assess bot-related signals; JevShield classifies message content. They complement each other, and neither guarantees that every unwanted submission will be stopped.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • Added Protection Mode: Observe only and Block high-confidence spam; new setups default to Observe while configured upgrades keep blocking.
  • Added integration action reporting for Contact Form 7, WPForms, Elementor Pro Forms, and native comments.
  • Added persistent administrator quota warnings and accurate settings status for Observe mode and exhausted quota.
  • Reject invalid API responses safely and allow review verdicts through.
  • Clarified detection logs, transmitted metadata, quota usage, and false-positive limitations.

1.0.1

  • Added live API key connection health check and quota status directly on the Settings screen.
  • Added helpful onboarding banner for newly activated installations to guide API key setup.
  • Added direct Settings shortcut link on the Plugins administration page.
  • Improved rejection error messaging clarity across supported form builders.

1.0.0

  • Initial release of JevShield AI Anti-Spam for Forms.
